exit_trigger: Any integrity question emerges or cannot be resolved after scuttlebutt on management; Verified 15-point score falls below 11; R&D effectiveness or margin trend deteriorates; Share count dilution accelerates through equity financing; Scuttlebutt returns negative signals from customers, employees or competitors
rationale: I own this position: 50 shares bought at $15.18, now $16.44, up 8.3% after 185 days. The reported numbers are what I look for, with five-year revenue growth of 41.4%, an operating margin of 37.1%, R&D at 11.5% of revenue, and no reported debt. But my doctrine rests on management integrity, candor and depth, and the snapshot says nothing about any of them, so I cannot say the checklist is met. Missing evidence lowers my conviction; it does not prove a mistake, and a modest gain and a low P/E are not reasons to sell. I will keep the shares and add no capital until scuttlebutt on integrity and management is done. If that work turns up anything less than completely satisfactory, I will sell.

exit_trigger: Integrity question emerges, or integrity check is adversely resolved in further scuttlebutt; 15-point score, once fully evaluated, falls below 11; R&D effectiveness declines or R&D intensity is cut to hit near-term earnings; Share count reverses to meaningful dilution or an equity raise is announced; Management transition or culture deterioration evident in employee and customer feedback; Margin gains prove to be price-driven or one-off rather than cost-engineered
rationale: I own 40 shares bought at $23.98 and now worth $19.48, an unrealised loss of 18.76% after 185 days. A price decline is not one of my three reasons to sell. What the numbers do show is encouraging: a 20% share count reduction over five years, R&D at 20.3% of revenue, and margins up about 1,704 bps. But I could not check management integrity, sales organization, labor relations or candor from this data, and an unverified Point 15 means I would not add. I keep the position small, hold through the quarterly noise, and do the scuttlebutt work before I put more capital into it.

exit_trigger: Any integrity question about management emerges, including restatements, undisclosed related-party dealings or misleading disclosure; Scuttlebutt, once gathered, returns negative signals from customers, former employees or competitors; The 15-point score is shown to be below 11 when properly evaluated; R&D intensity (currently 23.55% of revenue) or the margin trend deteriorates materially; Further dilution: continued growth in share count that cancels shareholders' benefit from growth; A clearly superior opportunity appears (Fisher's third sell trigger)
rationale: I own this stock, and I will not sell it merely because I am up 17.77% since May, because gains alone are never my reason to sell. In this snapshot I cannot verify management integrity, customer retention, employee turnover, the industry margin benchmark or the accounting controls, so Point 15 is unproven and I will not add to the position until it is. A P/E of 11.83 is no reason to buy a business on cheapness, and no reason to sell it either. I hold, and I do the scuttlebutt work to see whether this deserves to stay.

rationale: I own this company, and what I can see of it is the kind of profile I look for: revenue compounding at 16.5% a year over five years, R&D at 17.3% of revenue, and an operating margin of 46.9% that has widened by about 688 basis points over five years.
